title: What a litigation hold is, and who should get one
author: Helena Corrowen
summary: When a dispute is likely, you must keep the relevant documents. Here is who to send the notice to and what it should say.
body:
A litigation hold is a written instruction to keep documents and data that relate to a dispute. Send it as soon as a lawsuit is reasonably likely, not when it is filed.

Who gets it

  • Everyone who worked on the deal or the dispute
  • IT, for email, chat and backups
  • Outside vendors who hold your data

Clients can find our hold template in the client library.

title: Non-compete changes: what employers should review this quarter
author: Odalys Fenwright
summary: A summary of recent (fictional) state legislative changes to restrictive covenants, with a review checklist.
body:
This alert describes fictional legislation for this example site. In the story, the state legislature limited non-competes for employees below a salary threshold.

Review

  • Which employees signed non-competes
  • Their current salaries
  • Whether a non-solicitation clause would protect the same interest

title: Operating agreements: five clauses that prevent lawsuits
author: Bram Ivesmark
summary: Deadlock, buy-sell, valuation, death and disability, and dispute resolution: what each clause should say.
body:
1. Deadlock. What happens when the members split evenly.
  2. Buy-sell. Who can buy whom, and when.
  3. Valuation. A formula, not a future argument.
  4. Death and disability. Insurance-funded where possible.
  5. Disputes. Mediation first, then a named forum.

title: Before you appeal: three questions we ask
author: Teodor Lund-Vashti
summary: Standard of review, preservation and cost. If the answers are wrong, an appeal rarely helps.
body: Was the issue preserved? What standard of review applies? And what does winning get you? We answer all three in a one-page memo before anyone files a notice of appeal.
